candidates.title: Franklin Arrives in Philadelphia with Three Rolls of Bread
candidates.rights_status_quote: This eBook is for the use of anyone anywhere at no cost and with almost no restrictions whatsoever. You may copy it, give it away or re-use it under the terms of the Project Gutenberg License included with this eBook or online at www.gutenberg.net
candidates.rights_reasoning: Project Gutenberg explicitly permits copying and re-use under its license; the underlying autobiography is a public-domain work by Benjamin Franklin. ([gutenberg.org](https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/148/pg148.html))
candidates.story_fit_reason: Franklin’s hungry, awkward arrival in Philadelphia—walking through the streets with bread under his arms—offers a vivid, self-contained episode about a young traveler beginning a new life.
candidates.concern: Use Franklin’s original narrative rather than relying on the 1909 editor’s introduction or notes.

candidates.title: A Confederate Stableman Changes Sides
candidates.rights_status_quote: This work is in the public domain in the United States because it was published before January 1, 1931.
candidates.rights_reasoning: Wikisource explicitly marks the 1869 publication as public domain in the United States, allowing its text to be adapted there. ([en.wikisource.org](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Autobiography_of_a_Scalawag))
candidates.story_fit_reason: The narrator’s decision to abandon the Confederate stables, board a Union transport, and persuade General Butler that he is a persecuted Union man creates a compact escape-and-improvisation story.
candidates.concern: The author is unidentified and the piece may use satire or exaggeration, so its historical reliability needs checking.

candidates.title: A Missouri Diarist’s Wartime Life
candidates.rights_status_quote: This work was published before January 1, 1931, and is in the public domain worldwide because the author died at least 100 years ago.
candidates.rights_reasoning: Wikisource explicitly identifies the work as worldwide public domain and notes that it is a diary of John Jay Johns. ([en.wikisource.org](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/A_Short_History_of_My_Life))
candidates.story_fit_reason: A first-person diary can be mined for one sharply bounded entry—such as a journey, wartime hardship, or tense personal encounter—and recast in simple English without needing a broad historical summary.
candidates.concern: The Wikisource text is a copy of a copy, so the original diary and a specific episode should be checked against the Missouri Historical Society record.
